items.question: How much does a project cost?
items.answer: It depends on what you need built. A focused website costs far less than a full platform with an admin panel and a mobile app. After a short discovery call about how your business runs today, we deliver a written quote with a clear scope, exact timeline, and a fixed price for each phase—so you know the full investment before any work starts.

items.question: How long until we launch?
items.answer: A focused website usually ships in 2 to 4 weeks. A full platform, such as a business management system, a customer app or an online marketplace, typically takes a few months. We commit to a clear timeline in the quote, and you test working software along the way every week so the launch date never comes as a surprise.

items.question: Who owns the code when it is done?
items.answer: You own 100% of the code, intellectual property, and infrastructure accounts from day one. When the project completes, you receive the full repository, documentation, and credentials. There are zero licensing traps or vendor lock-in.

items.question: Can you work with our existing system?
items.answer: Usually, yes. Most businesses already rely on tools they don't want to replace, such as a POS counter, payment gateway, online store, or accounting software. We build modern integrations to connect new software directly to those tools so data flows automatically instead of being typed twice. If a replacement serves you better, we explain why first.

items.question: What time zone do you work in?
items.answer: Our engineering hub is based in Dhaka, Bangladesh (GMT+6). We schedule our work hours to guarantee at least 4 to 6 hours of daily overlap with clients across Europe, Asia-Pacific, and the Americas for smooth meetings and real-time Slack communication.

posts.title: How much does a POS system cost for a small shop?
posts.summary: What a point of sale system really costs a small shop: the monthly software fee, card processing fees, hardware investments, and when a custom system saves thousands over subscriptions.
posts.searchTitle: POS System Cost for a Small Shop

body.text: For most small shops, a POS system costs between nothing and a few hundred dollars a month in software, plus a processing fee of roughly 2.3% to 3% on every card transaction, plus a one-time hardware cost ranging from $60 for a basic card reader to over $1,000 for a full counter register. While shop owners typically compare monthly software subscriptions first, card processing percentages are usually where most of the money actually goes.

body.heading: The three costs you will always pay
body.text: Every POS setup consists of three core components: 1) The software subscription, which often starts free for single registers and escalates as you add multi-location inventory and staff permissions. 2) The card processing fee deducted from every customer swipe or tap. 3) The physical hardware, including card readers, tablet stands, receipt printers, cash drawers, and barcode scanners. Always sum all three costs together before comparing platforms.

body.heading: What popular systems charge in 2026
body.text: In 2026, entry-level Square plans start free with paid tiers around $49/month per location, taking 2.4% to 2.6% + 15¢ per transaction. Shopify POS Pro averages $89/month per location, while Lightspeed retail starts around $89/month on annual commitments. Clover and Toast operate in comparable brackets depending on custom hardware financing. Since pricing structures shift frequently, always calculate fees against your exact sales volume.

body.heading: The card fee is the real hidden cost
body.text: Consider a retail shop generating $20,000 a month in card transactions. At a 2.5% processing rate, you pay $500 every single month in processing alone—ten times the cost of a standard $49 monthly software license. When evaluating POS options, negotiating or optimizing your payment gateway rate saves dramatically more capital than switching base software tiers.

body.heading: Hidden subscription traps to ask about
body.text: Always inquire about hidden charges before signing multi-year agreements: extra fees for multiple registers, paid add-ons for customer loyalty or barcode inventory, contract cancellation penalties, and data export restrictions. Several proprietary vendors lock your customer history and product catalogs behind difficult proprietary formats if you ever decide to leave.

body.heading: When a custom POS starts saving you money
body.text: An off-the-shelf POS fits most single-outlet boutiques. However, a custom POS built on open web standards pays off when you manage multiple warehouses, sell through field distributors, need live sync with custom accounting software, or pay thousands annually for bloated SaaS features you never touch. One purpose-built system tailored to your exact workflow eliminates recurrent seat licenses and protects your margins permanently.

posts.title: When to move your orders off WhatsApp
posts.summary: WhatsApp is great for early sales, but breaks down as order volume grows. Here are the 4 unmistakable signs you've outgrown chat orders, and how a dedicated ordering system protects your revenue.

body.text: You should move your customer orders off WhatsApp when messages start getting buried during peak hours, only one person holds all customer details, or your team spends more time transcribing chats into notebooks and spreadsheets than fulfilling orders. WhatsApp is unmatched for customer conversations, but it was never designed to operate as an inventory or order management database.

body.heading: Why WhatsApp works so well at the start
body.text: At launch, WhatsApp is unbeatable: every customer already has the app installed, it costs zero dollars to operate, and communication feels warm and personal. For boutique bakers, home kitchens, or emerging retailers, taking orders over direct chat is a completely sensible way to validate demand.

body.heading: Sign 1: Orders get missed during peak hours
body.text: When a busy evening floods your inbox with dozens of concurrent chats, messages inevitably slip out of view. A missed order is not only lost revenue—it is an unhappy customer who will order from a competitor next time. Missed messages almost always happen on your highest-potential sales days.

body.heading: Sign 2: Your entire business lives on one phone
body.text: If the person holding the WhatsApp phone takes a sick day, goes on holiday, or leaves the company, your entire sales pipeline freezes. Nobody else knows who paid, what was dispatched, or which orders are pending. A sustainable business cannot depend on a single mobile device.

body.heading: Sign 3: You copy every order twice
body.text: When staff manually type order details from chat bubbles into spreadsheets, kitchen tickets, or courier slips, human error is guaranteed. Every typo in a delivery address or item quantity wastes time, damages food, and burns customer trust.

body.heading: Sign 4: You cannot answer basic business questions
body.text: Which three menu items drove 60% of your revenue last month? How many repeat customers ordered on Friday? What was your average basket value? Chat message histories cannot generate business intelligence or automated sales reports.

body.heading: What a dedicated ordering system changes
body.text: With a dedicated web ordering system, customers browse an interactive digital menu, pick item variants, and pay online. Orders route instantly to kitchen displays or packing stations, receipts generate automatically, and inventory updates in real time. You still maintain WhatsApp for high-touch customer care—and can even automate shipping updates directly to their WhatsApp.

posts.title: A checklist before you buy clinic software
posts.summary: Twelve critical questions to ask before buying appointment, patient record, or prescription software—so you invest in a system your doctors and reception staff actually enjoy using.

body.text: Before purchasing clinical management software, verify four fundamentals: it fits how your practice already runs, patient records remain strictly private and portable, staff can learn it in hours, and total three-year ownership costs are transparent. Use this 12-point checklist with every vendor you evaluate.

body.heading: 1. Fit with your real clinical workflows
body.text: 1. Does the software accommodate your appointment types, multiple doctor consult schedules, and walk-in queues the way you operate today? 2. Can patients easily book, reschedule, and receive automated SMS/WhatsApp reminders online? 3. Does it support digital prescriptions, diagnostic lab orders, and specialist referrals in formats your physicians already use?

body.heading: 2. Patient data privacy, HIPAA, and GDPR
body.text: 4. Where is confidential patient data hosted, and who maintains access rights? Demand granular role-based access control so front-desk receptionists cannot view confidential clinical diagnosis notes. 5. Does the platform satisfy regional privacy regulations (HIPAA in the US, GDPR in Europe, and national data laws)? 6. Can you export full patient medical histories in open, standard formats at any time without fees?

body.heading: 3. Day-to-day front-desk speed
body.text: 7. Can your reception desk master the daily check-in flow in less than a single afternoon? Always insist on a live trial with your actual clinic staff. 8. Does the software operate smoothly on existing hardware, and does it support offline caching if the internet drops? 9. Is there an optimized mobile view for doctors moving between consult rooms and surgical suites?

body.heading: 4. True cost, response times, and time-zone support
body.text: 10. What is your total three-year expenditure including onboarding, custom report templates, and extra doctor seats? 11. When a critical booking outage occurs, what is the guaranteed emergency response SLA, and is support available in your working time zone? 12. Does it bridge cleanly into your lab, pharmacy, and accounting tools, or will staff manually re-type patient invoices?

body.heading: 5. Off-the-shelf software vs. a custom clinic system
body.text: Commercial off-the-shelf software works well for solo practitioner clinics. However, a custom system built around your exact workflow becomes far more cost-effective when you manage multiple outpatient branches, run an on-site diagnostic laboratory or pharmacy, or constantly fight software built for generic hospital networks.

seo.description: How Devs Recipe collects, uses and deletes the personal data you send us through our forms.

sections.heading: What we collect
sections.text: We only collect information you voluntarily provide. From our contact form, we collect your name, work email, business type, budget range, and project brief solely to respond to your inquiry. From the newsletter, we collect your email address exclusively for monthly updates (with one-click unsubscribe anytime). For job applications, we collect your name, email, phone number, portfolio link, and CV to evaluate employment opportunities. All submissions are processed securely through encrypted endpoints. We never sell, rent, or trade your personal data.

sections.heading: How long we keep it
sections.text: Contact and newsletter data is retained only for the duration of our business communication or until you request its deletion. Job applicant data is retained for up to 12 months with your consent for future openings, after which it is permanently purged.

sections.heading: Your rights
sections.text: You have the right to request access to the personal data we hold about you, request corrections, or ask for complete deletion at any time. Simply email devsrecipe@gmail.com and we will process and confirm your request within 30 days. If you reside in the European Union or the United Kingdom, you additionally hold the right to lodge a complaint with your local data protection supervisory authority.
